evals.prompt: Using the code-review-and-quality process, evaluate this change request: a single pull request contains a 1400-line diff that refactors the existing payment module's error handling AND adds a brand-new refund feature with its own tests. Should this be reviewed as-is or split, and how?
evals.expected_output: Recommends splitting the refactor from the new feature into separate changes, citing the ~1000-line size guidance and the rule that refactors and feature work are two changes.

evals.prompt: Using the code-review-and-quality severity labeling system, write review comments for this Go change: it adds a new exported function with no doc comment, and separately removes an authorization check that verified the caller owned the resource before deleting it. Label each finding appropriately.
evals.expected_output: Labels the missing authorization check as Critical (blocks merge) and the missing doc comment as Nit or Optional, using the prefix system from the skill.

assertions.text: Labels the authorization removal as Critical
Labels the missing doc comment as a minor/nit item
Does not treat both findings as equally required

evals.prompt: Using the code-review-and-quality guidance on change descriptions, review whether this commit message is acceptable for merge: "Fix bug". If not, explain why and give a better one-line example for a change that fixes a null pointer panic when a user has no profile photo set.
evals.expected_output: Rejects "Fix bug" as an anti-pattern and proposes a specific, imperative, standalone replacement describing the actual fix.

assertions.text: Flags the description as an anti-pattern
